newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican drug lord's prison term extended.
newsitem.headline: Mexican drug lord's prison term extended.

text.p: One of Mexico's most feared drug criminals had his prison term extended seven more years on Friday, meaning he should be behind bars for at least 20 years and nine months, officials said.
The sentencing is a real and symbolic victory for Mexico's anti-drugs effort as it reverses a recent trend in which drug criminals have been let off with minor sentences.
Judges are believed to be swayed either by bribes or threats from the ruthless narcotics cartels.

Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman, former head of the Sinaloa cartel, was sentenced to seven years and nine months for bribery and criminal association, Mexican Attorney General's Office (PGR) said in a statement.
Guzman was found to have bribed federal agents in exchange for protection, the PGR said.
He has been jailed in the western state of Jalisco since June 18, 1993, on drug trafficking charges.

Authorities believe Guzman in May 1993 was the intended target of a bungled "hit" by members of a rival drug gang who instead shot to death Roman Catholic Cardinal Juan Jesus Posados Ocampo in a case of mistaken identity at Guadalajara airport.
The cardinal and the drug lord were chauffered in similar cars.
Guzman was rounded up from information obtained in the probe into the cardinal's death, the PGR said.
The bribery and criminal association charges had been dismissed by another judge earlier this year, but prosecutors appealed, leading to Friday's sentence by a judge in Jalisco, the PGR said.
The most famous example of drug lords getting off easy is that of Hector "The Blond" Palma, who was sentenced to six years on weapons charges and later had his term reduced to 2 1/2 years.
The PGR has condemned the light sentence for Palma, and some legal experts have called for reforms that would protect judges who oversee cases of high-profile drug defendants.
According to U.S. estimates, drug cartels spend $6 billion a year bribing Mexican authorities in exchange for protection.
